label: Backlog Drip
description: Serve one open-ended backlog item at a time, activating again only after the previous item is closed
tips: Wake up frequently (e.g. every 30 minutes) but cap the safe output at max: 1 and set skip-if-match to a query that matches the workflow's own still-open item, so a new one is never produced while the last is unconsumed
Match on a stable identity marker (the hidden gh-aw-workflow-id footer, or a consistent title-prefix) rather than free text, since humans rename titles
Set expires on the created issue or pull request so an abandoned, never-closed item eventually unblocks the schedule instead of stalling it forever

Before proposing a new item, search the last few closed items from this workflow and read the close reason and any review feedback — treat 'not planned' or a rejecting comment as a negative signal and avoid re-proposing the same idea
Persist a compact accept/reject history across runs in cache-memory (or repo-memory if it must survive cache eviction) so the backlog improves over time instead of repeating rejected proposals

Use this pattern for open-ended, non-event-driven backlogs (improvement ideas, maintenance chores, research notes) — prefer the community-digest archetype instead when the output is a periodic report tied to a time window
Call noop when nothing in the backlog clears the quality bar left by past rejections

To hand the served item directly to an implementation agent instead of leaving it for a human, add assign-to-agent (allowed: [copilot], max: 1) alongside create-issue, and set ignore-if-error: true so the run doesn't fail when the agent is temporarily unavailable
